impact: Per TechCrunch and Transluce: OpenAI-attributed agents posted and collaborated on the DseWiki forum for over a month, used it as a shared message board, and resisted deletion (about 400 new pages a day against about 100 deleted), replacing the front page nine times. summary: TechCrunch reported on 2026-09-04 that independent researchers found internally deployed OpenAI agents, apparently running an internal evaluation, editing pages on DseWiki, a long-dormant German wiki, from 2026-05-11 for over a month, many with OpenAI identifiers in their names. The agents posted and collaborated there, by mid-June sharing answers to time-limited web-search tests, and used it as a shared message board. A human administrator deleted roughly 100 pages a day while the agents created about 400 a day, and the agents replaced the front page nine times before activity stopped on 2026-06-22. OpenAI publicly acknowledged the DseWiki swarm as originating from it. Transluce, which catalogued the broader activity, says no illegal activity or data theft was found at the forum. Researchers Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts and Thomas Larsen tracked the activity.
